symbols.def: \(G_S(M)\) is obtained from the minimal structural graph whose parent relations are functional dependencies outside exogenous null sets, tested over all endogenous input assignments including assignments off the observational support, by retaining \(S\), latent-projecting, and applying selected-MAG projection

symbols.def: \(R_{\max}=\max_{\mathsf a}\prod_{j\in W}r_j^{(\prod_{i\in\operatorname{pa}_{\mathsf a}(j)}r_i)(m+3)^{d_{\mathsf a}(j)}}\), where \(\mathsf a\) ranges over the finite labeled architectures and \(d_{\mathsf a}(j)\) is the number of child-set sources incident to \(j\)

symbols.name: T
symbols.type: finite directed architecture with exogenous sources indexed by nonempty child sets
symbols.space: architectures compatible with at least one graph in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\)

symbols.type: product of source-simplex mass vectors for architecture \(T\)
symbols.space: the finite product of probability simplexes for the sources and response types of \(T\)

symbols.name: Iess
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_T=\{\operatorname{dir}(i,j):i,j\in W,\ i\ne j\}\cup\{\operatorname{src}(C,j):\varnothing\ne C\subseteq W,\ j\in C\}\), with \(|\mathcal I_T|\le N(N-1)+N2^{N-1}\); source indices are their canonical child sets \(C\), so \(\mathcal I_T\) is invariant to source-value, source-order, and response-label permutations

symbols.name: Ze
symbols.type: nonnegative essential-feature polynomial indexed by \(e\in\mathcal I_T\)
symbols.def: For \(e=\operatorname{dir}(i,j)\), \(Z_e(T,p_T)\) sums the probability of exogenous response contexts for which the table of \(j\) differs at some two endogenous parent assignments that differ only at \(i\), with the existential comparison ranging over every table input including off-support assignments. For \(e=\operatorname{src}(C,j)\), it sums over two positive-mass values of the child-set source \(U_C\) and the other-source contexts for which the table of \(j\) differs at some endogenous input assignment. Each summand is a zero-one table indicator times a monomial in \(p_T\).

symbols.name: PsiTG
symbols.def: \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\) is obtained by declaring exactly the primitive structural features \(e\in\mathcal I_T\) with \(Z_e(T,p_T)>0\), declaring the remaining features by \(Z_e(T,p_T)=0\), and applying the finite latent-and-selection projection rules; it is true exactly when the projected graph equals \(G\)

symbols.name: Fdelta

symbols.name: Cert
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) is either a rational-univariate representation of a satisfying branch of \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\), or one sign-invariant cylindrical cell certificate for each enumerated \(T,G\) proving that its conjunction in \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) is empty

standard.name: Strict positivity of the selected observational kernel
Exact selected-MAG membership in a COPAG equivalence class
Compatibility with a selected multinomial law up to its common normalization

novel.justification: The lower bound is a calibrated sensitivity restriction on the population fraction entering the selected cohort. In survivor-selected studies it can be varied over values compatible with registry counts of eligible operations and observed discharge-alive records; it is not labeled as ordinary overlap or used merely to make a denominator positive.

The lower bound limits how much the intervention may reduce survival or ascertainment. It can be calibrated from a clinically defensible minimum discharge-alive rate under \(do(B=b)\), informed by external outcome surveillance or trial safety data; the mathematical domain requirement for \(n_M/d_M\) is only \(d_M>0\).

definitions.name: Exact selection-COPAG compatibility class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=\{M:\exists\rho\in[\delta,1]\text{ such that }G_S(M)\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P),\ c_v(M)=\rho q(v)\text{ for every }v\in\Omega_V,\text{ and }d_M\ge\delta\}\).

definitions.name: Graph-indexed response architecture list
definitions.construction: Enumerate a topological order on \(W\), a subset of its \(N(N-1)/2\) forward directed slots, and a subset of the \(2^N-1\) nonempty child sets indexing independent exogenous sources. This produces at most \(A_{\max}=N!\,2^{N(N-1)/2+2^N-1}\) labeled architectures before duplicate removal. For each architecture enumerate all deterministic tables, bounded by \(R_{\max}\), using at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) values per source, and retain each projected selected MAG \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\).

definitions.name: Exact graph-legality stratum
definitions.construction: For each pair \(T,G\), form \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\) from the complete invariant index \(\mathcal I_T\): use \(Z_e(T,p_T)>0\) exactly for the actual directed-parent and source-child incidences, use \(Z_e(T,p_T)=0\) for their complements, and mechanically compute latent-and-selection projection. The table comparisons defining \(Z_e\) range over all endogenous inputs, including configurations outside the observational support.

definitions.name: Finite graph-legal response fiber
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=\bigcup_T\{(p_T,\rho):p_T\text{ satisfies the exact graph-legality stratum},\ \Phi_T(p_T)_{c_v}=\rho q(v)\text{ for every }v\in\Omega_V,\ \delta\le\rho\le1,\ \Phi_T(p_T)_d\ge\delta\}\).

definitions.name: Certified finite legality procedure
definitions.construction: Generate the architecture list, expand every coordinate of \(\Phi_T\) and every \(Z_e\) as a rational polynomial, introduce \(t\) through \(\Phi_T(p_T)_n-t\Phi_T(p_T)_d=0\), and form \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) as the finite disjunction over \(T\) and \(G\in\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\). Quantifier elimination partitions the \(t\)-line, reports INFEASIBLE or isolates the algebraic infimum and supremum of the bounded finite image, and tests \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\) at each isolated closure endpoint. Cylindrical algebraic decomposition returns \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\): either an algebraic legal response witness, or sign-invariant cells proving each architecture branch empty and separating an illegal closure endpoint from every enumerated legal lift.

definitions.name: Sharp intervention compatibility fiber
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=\{\theta(M):M\in\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\}\), with the output INFEASIBLE when \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Essential-witness legal-lifting handle
definitions.construction: Start from the selection-aware canonical DAG transformations of Carey et al., retain the unnormalized selection coordinates in the moment map, partition each exogenous input by the full response tables of Duarte et al., and adapt the sourcewise support reduction of Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe by carrying positive essential-parent and inducing-path witness strata; at a vanishing witness boundary, search all COPAG-allowed architectures for an equal-moment legal representative.

statements.statement: Fix an enumerated finite architecture \(T\), its deterministic tables, and source masses \(p_T\). For every \(i,j\in W\), the minimal structural graph has the directed edge \(i\to j\) if and only if \(Z_{\operatorname{dir}(i,j)}(T,p_T)>0\). For every nonempty child-set index \(C\subseteq W\) and \(j\in C\), its source \(U_C\) is an actual parent of \(j\) if and only if \(Z_{\operatorname{src}(C,j)}(T,p_T)>0\). The endogenous table comparisons include assignments off the observational support, while the exogenous contexts are integrated under \(p_T\). Therefore \(G_S(M_{T,p_T})=G\) if and only if \(\Psi_{T,G}(p_T)\), and this equivalence is unchanged by permutations of source values, response labels, or sources having the same child-set index.
statements.justification: This lemma makes actual-edge legality a complete finite polynomial test rather than an informal list of permitted slots.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. encode a supplied graph, and Yang et al. encode PAG masks; neither gives an invariant if-and-only-if polynomial test for the exact selected MAG with off-support functional dependence.
statements.consumer: The certified bounding procedure uses the equivalence to reject response programs whose zero-mass limits silently delete a parent or confounding source.

statements.statement: Identical exogenous child sets can be merged without changing any structural solution, giving at most \(H_{\max}=2^N-1\) independent sources. On any fixed permitted architecture, sourcewise barycentric reduction preserves \(\zeta(M)\) with at most \(K_{\max}=m+3\) values per source. Every point of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) induces an SCM in \(\mathfrak M_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\), and, by the essential-feature lemma, the image of \(\mathfrak F_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is exactly the target-value set of the enumerated bounded finite SCMs satisfying actual selected-MAG legality. No claim here says that ordinary barycentric reduction preserves legality or that every arbitrary admissible SCM belongs to this bounded class.
statements.justification: This theorem separates the valid finite moment reduction from the still-open graph-legal lifting step and provides a sound bounded response language.
statements.gap: The source-merging and barycentric components are informed by Evans, Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe, and Duarte et al.; their results do not preserve strict functional-essentiality witnesses under support deletion.
statements.consumer: It supplies the finite candidate language used to audit selection-sensitive bounds in the FCI and LV-IDA workflow of Lee et al.

statements.statement: For every finite rational instance, the certified procedure enumerates at most \(A_{\max}=N!\,2^{N(N-1)/2+2^N-1}\) labeled source architectures, enumerates their deterministic response tables up to \(R_{\max}\), and expands the moment and essential-feature formulas coefficient by coefficient. Quantifier elimination reports INFEASIBLE or isolates the algebraic infimum and supremum of the bounded finite graph-legal image. At each isolated endpoint \(t\), it decides \(\mathsf{Lift}(t)\). If true, \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) contains an algebraic \(T,p_T,\rho\) witness whose exact graph is verified by \(\Psi_{T,G}\). If false, \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) contains a finite family of sign-invariant cylindrical cells proving that every enumerated legal branch is empty, so the closure endpoint has no legal lift in any enumerated architecture. With parameter count \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}\), constraint count \(s_{\mathrm{count}}\), maximum degree \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}\), and expanded coefficient bit length \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\), the arithmetic-operation bound is \(A_{\max}R_{\max}(s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{2^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}}\operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}})\).
statements.justification: The procedure produces checkable positive or negative legality certificates rather than restating attainment as existential feasibility.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. optimize a compact fixed-graph parameterization but do not enumerate exact selected-MAG strata or certify that a boundary optimum is excluded from every legal architecture.
statements.consumer: A clinical audit can distinguish an attained endpoint mechanism from a graph-deleting closure artifact and retain the certificate with the reported bound.

statements.statement: Does \(q(v)>0\) for every \(v\in\Omega_V\), together with the calibrated restrictions \(\rho\ge\delta\) and \(d_M\ge\delta\), imply both that every moment vector of an arbitrary admissible SCM has an equal-moment representative in the bounded finite legal fiber and that every limiting vector of bounded graph-legal moments has an equal-moment finite SCM whose actual selected MAG remains in \(\mathcal G(\mathcal P)\)? Resolve first the binary three-observed-variable COPAG with a compelled collider by stratifying the invariant essential-feature polynomials \(Z_e\). An affirmative resolution must give a legal lift for every boundary stratum; a negative resolution must give a positive rational \(q\), a rational \(\delta\), and an algebraic endpoint for which the negative certificate \(\mathsf{Cert}(t)\) excludes every legal architecture.
statements.justification: This is the sole nonroutine topological bottleneck between exact graph semantics and attained sharp bounds.
statements.gap: Boeken, Forré, and Mooij show faithful laws form an open dense set, but their topology neither supplies an equal-moment lift on the unfaithful boundary nor produces an unattained causal endpoint.
statements.consumer: Its answer determines whether exact-graph selection-COPAG bounds may be reported as attained sharp extrema without adding faithfulness or a minimum edge-strength condition.

statements.statement: If the universal legal-lifting property in Open-ended Question 1 holds, then every nonempty \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \([h_-,h_+]\), hence a finite union of closed intervals and points; \(\ell\) and \(u\) are attained algebraic numbers and admit finite response-SCM witnesses. With \(H_{\max}=2^N-1\), source support bounded by \(K_{\max}=m+3\), parameter count \(p_{\mathrm{dim}}=O(H_{\max}K_{\max})\), constraint count \(s_{\mathrm{count}}=O(m+H_{\max}K_{\max}+N^3)\), degree \(D_{\mathrm{deg}}=O(H_{\max}+N)\), and expanded coefficient bit length \(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\), cylindrical algebraic decomposition gives the per-architecture factor \((s_{\mathrm{count}}D_{\mathrm{deg}})^{2^{O(p_{\mathrm{dim}})}}\operatorname{poly}(\tau_{\mathrm{eff}})\) in the certified procedure.
statements.justification: Compactness converts the algebraic compiler into sharp, attained causal conclusions and explicit certificates.
statements.gap: Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe derive closed semialgebraic correlation sets after cardinality reduction, but exact selected-MAG inequalities and shared selection normalization are absent.
statements.consumer: Attained algebraic witnesses allow auditors to display concrete best- and worst-case mechanisms rather than numerical optimizer traces.

statements.statement: If \(\mathcal P\) is the complete all-circle COPAG, every observed variable has at least two states, and \(|\Omega_B|\ge2\), then \(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)=[L_\delta,U_\delta]\), where \(L_\delta\) and \(U_\delta\) are given by the closed-form saturated envelope. Both endpoints are attained by a one-source SCM with at most \(m+1\) positive-mass response types. If \(h\) is constant, the interval is the singleton \(\{h_-\}\); if the intervention is vacuous, the fiber is the singleton \(\{\sum_{v\in\Omega_V}q(v)h(A(v))\}\).
statements.justification: The closed form is an exact benchmark that exposes how the selection margin, factual treated cells, and outcome range determine the bound.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. provide a general polynomial program, but not this analytic selection-margin formula over a saturated COPAG.
statements.consumer: It gives a transparent sensitivity curve in \(\delta\) for screening intervention claims before running the general compiler.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal P^*\), \(q^*=(1,2,3,4)/10\), \(\delta^*=1/4\), intervention \(do(B=0)\), and \(h^*(a)=a\), the sharp fiber is \(\Theta_{\delta^*}(\mathcal P^*,q^*)=[1/20,39/40]\). The lower and upper endpoints are attained by five response types with masses \((1,2,3,4,30)/40\), common-source selected-MAG legality, and intervention-specific selection probability one.
statements.justification: The witness is an exact arithmetic regression test for both the formula and the graph-legality implementation.
statements.gap: No named comparator reports this selected-law and selection-margin instance or its two attained response constructions.
statements.consumer: Implementers can reject a compiler that returns anything other than \([1/20,39/40]\) or fails to recover endpoint SCMs.

statements.statement: There exists a positive selected law on two binary observed variables and a one-parameter family of finite SCMs with constant moment vector \(\zeta(M)\) such that the SCM has a common-source bidirected edge for every interior parameter value and loses that edge at both boundary values. Therefore, preservation of \(\zeta(M)\) alone does not preserve exact graph legality, although the boundary moment vector has a distinct legal lift.
statements.justification: The proposition rules out the tempting but invalid inference from Carathéodory moment preservation to exact-edge preservation.
statements.gap: Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe preserve observed behavior, not functional essentiality; this example identifies the first proof step that must change.
statements.consumer: It prevents a bounding package from certifying graph legality solely from preserved observational and query moments.

statements.statement: Suppose \(\Pr(q\in C_n)\ge1-\alpha_q\) and \(\Pr(\mathcal P\in\Pi_n)\ge1-\alpha_g\). Then the confidence fiber satisfies \(\Pr(\Theta_\delta(\mathcal P,q)\subseteq\widehat{\mathfrak C}_n)\ge1-\alpha_q-\alpha_g\) without differentiability, compactness, or a unique active optimizer. In the saturated binary witness, simultaneous one-sided exact binomial lower limits \(l_{01}\) and \(l_{00}\), each with error allocation \(\alpha_q/2\), yield the finite-sample interval \([\delta l_{01},1-\delta l_{00}]\) covering the entire sharp fiber with probability at least \(1-\alpha_q\).
statements.justification: Finite-sample event inclusion remains valid at singular active faces, unattained endpoints, and collapsed identification intervals.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer treat a fixed criterion, Imbens and Manski treat interval endpoints, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky treat post-discovery point effects; none covers a learned selection-COPAG compatibility fiber.
statements.consumer: The method attaches calibrated uncertainty to the graph and effect ambiguity in the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery FCI and LV-IDA analysis.

sampling_model.design: An independent sample \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is drawn from the selected multinomial law \(q\); an optional COPAG confidence set is produced from the same sample by a coverage-valid discovery procedure.
sampling_model.units: Each sampled unit is one retained clinical visit with finite coded variables \(V\); the population SCM also contains the binary selection variable \(S\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query is the hard intervention \(do(B=b)\); the intervention is hypothetical and sampling randomness comes from the selected observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every selected cell is positive under \(q\). The common lower bound \(\delta\) on population and post-intervention selection is a calibrated sensitivity restriction, not a standard overlap label; the conditional estimand itself only requires \(d_M>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(q\) by a simultaneous multinomial confidence region and propagate graph uncertainty by union over a COPAG confidence set; no faithfulness assumption is imposed on the identification class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 equates a fixed canonical-DAG discrete causal bounding problem with minimization and maximization of a polynomial program.
Theorem 3 states that optimal neural counterfactual bounds and optimal PAG counterfactual bounds coincide under a faithful observational law.
Theorem 4.13 gives equality of marginal DAG models for DAGs with the same latent projection, and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection.
Proposition 2 replaces one latent source by at most \(d+1\) values without changing the observed network behavior.
Equality of selected-marginalized directed graphs is equivalent to indistinguishability under the Observe-and-Do probing scheme.
Theorem 4.15 gives completeness of sIDP and the causal calculus for unconditional interventional kernels under a COPAG.
Theorem 5 states that faithful distributions are nonempty, open, and dense in the total-variation Markov model.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as the identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

tldr: A positive selected law need not be faithful, and exact graphical strata are open because an actual parent or shared source can disappear when a response mass approaches zero. The project indexes every primitive functional-essentiality feature by directed vertex pairs and invariant source child sets, proves that explicit nonnegative polynomial signs are equivalent to the exact selected MAG even when dependence occurs only at off-support endogenous inputs, and compiles bounded finite response strata. A certified procedure enumerates at most \(N!\,2^{N(N-1)/2+2^N-1}\) architectures and returns either an algebraic legal endpoint witness or a cell certificate excluding every enumerated legal lift. Universal legal lifting for arbitrary positive, potentially unfaithful selected laws remains the open kernel. The population and post-intervention \(\delta\) margins are calibrated sensitivity restrictions, while inference is limited to finite-sample outer coverage. The saturated binary case has the attained sharp interval \(\left[1/20,39/40\right]\), providing a regression test and an audit target for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery analysis of Lee et al.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give complete point identification for COPAGs under selection, Yang et al. optimize over PAG-compatible neural SCMs under faithfulness, and Duarte et al. give sharp polynomial programs for a fixed canonical DAG. None characterizes closure or attainment after imposing the actual, rather than merely permitted, selected-MAG stratum for a positive but potentially unfaithful selected law.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the graph-legal compatibility fiber: a finite union of semialgebraic response-function strata whose invariant essential-feature signs determine the selected MAG and whose boundary losses are either repaired by an equal-moment legal lift or exposed by a negative certificate.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and an if-and-only-if polynomial legality lemma, a bounded finite stratum compiler, and a certificate-producing architecture-enumeration procedure. It isolates universal graph-legal lifting as the load-bearing open question, resolves its compelled-collider kill test first, and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence.

related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning. Evans's Theorem 4.13 canonicalizes latent DAG margins and Proposition 7.3 makes latent projection commute with intervention, but these results identify model equivalence rather than closure of an exact functional-essentiality stratum. Carey et al. characterize selected interventional indistinguishability by selected-marginalized directed graphs; their normalized selected models do not fix the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities used for sensitivity calibration here. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe's Proposition 2 gives sourcewise Carathéodory reduction, while the exclusive-or diagnostic shows why moment preservation alone can destroy an actual shared source. Duarte et al.'s Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 give finite full-response disturbance models and polynomial sharp bounds for a fixed canonical DAG; the present work is informed by that encoding and adds an invariant exact-MAG sign test and negative certificates across all enumerated COPAG architectures. Yang et al. characterize PAG-compatible SCMs under faithfulness but do not treat selection or zero-mask closure. Chen and Mooij give complete COPAG point identification under selection and leave sharp discrete bounds open. Boeken, Forré, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not supply an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary. Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky inform confidence-set inversion; the formal inference result here is only finite-sample outer coverage. Lee et al. provide the clinical consumer: FCI and LV-IDA are applied after conditioning on discharge alive, with acknowledged selection bias and graph ambiguity.
technical_internal_limitation: The binary exclusive-or family in the moment-compression warning holds the positive selected law and intervention moment fixed while a common-source edge disappears at both support boundaries. Thus an individual graph-legal parameter stratum is not closed, and moment-preserving support deletion is not a proof of exact-graph compactness. This diagnostic is not a claim that the fiber endpoint is unattained, because the same boundary moments have a distinct legal lift.
honest_scope: Source merging by identical child set, moment-preserving finite support on a fixed permitted architecture, exact polynomial legality for a finite response model, the saturated interval, certified feasibility within the bounded architecture list, and finite-sample confidence-set event inclusion are theorem targets. Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded exact-stratum compiler, preservation of unnormalized selection probabilities through canonicalization, and universal graph-legal lifting for positive unfaithful \(q\) remain open. No general Hausdorff, Painlevé--Kuratowski, or endpoint-convergence claim is made. If the compelled-collider test produces an unattained endpoint certified outside every legal architecture, compactness is withdrawn and the certified attainment frontier is the main result. Under a complete all-circle COPAG the formula reduces to bounded-outcome missing-selection logic; for a vacuous intervention it reduces to \(\mathbb E_q[h(A)]\).

seed_details.anchor: Evans2016Margins, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.3; CareyEtAl2025smDG, Sections 4--6
seed_details.opportunity: Strengthen selection-aware canonicalization from equality of normalized interventional models to preservation and closure of the exact selected-MAG moment fiber with absolute selection probabilities.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: After exogenizing latent vertices, retain \(S\) and the unnormalized cells \(\Pr(V=v,S=1)\); replace model-equivalence alone by a boundary lift that preserves every positive essential-feature polynomial.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for selection PAG sharp bounds, exact graph closure, selected-marginalized graph compatibility, and PAG SCM zero-mask boundaries found Chen and Mooij, Yang et al., Carey et al., Duarte et al., and Boeken et al., but no theorem for the target pair.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Evans and Carey et al. because their canonical graphs already preserve interventions under selection.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their preserved objects are marginal or normalized selected interventional models; the present fiber fixes absolute selection coordinates and actual functional-essentiality strata, which can be lost at support boundaries.

seed_details.anchor: BoekenForreMooij2026Faithful, Theorem 5 and Section 7; YangEtAl2026PAGSCM, Theorem 1
seed_details.opportunity: Give a necessary-and-sufficient polynomial criterion for closure of the binary three-variable compelled-collider fiber at positive unfaithful selected laws.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace density of faithful laws by explicit essential-parent strata and quantify over every COPAG-allowed completion at a limiting moment point.
seed_details.destination_search: A focused search for compelled-collider unfaithful closure and essential-parent polynomial strata located topology and PAG representation papers but no endpoint-attainment characterization.
seed_details.red_team: A three-node binary case is a toy witness with no general content.
seed_details.rebuttal: The result is an iff frontier over the entire positive law simplex for the minimal compelled feature, not a single tuned distribution, and it is the falsification gate for the general theorem.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive constructive source and response cardinality bounds while retaining exact graphical witnesses rather than moments alone.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Augment sourcewise barycentric compression with finite essentiality certificates and allow architecture switching at zero-witness faces.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for graph-preserving Carathéodory, latent cardinality with essential edges, and semialgebraic PAG response types found no bound preserving actual selected-MAG legality.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Carathéodory after adding graph indicators as moments.
seed_details.rebuttal: Common-source essentiality is polynomial, often quadratic in a source law, and strict positivity can vanish under ordinary linear moment compression; architecture switching is additional content.

seed_details.opportunity: Derive analytic saturated-COPAG endpoints as functions of \(\delta\), their sign-stability threshold, and exact finite-sample confidence limits.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use intervention consistency on the factual \(B=b,S=1\) cells before polynomial optimization, then solve the remaining response allocation in closed form.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for closed-form selection-margin PAG bounds found generic selection programs but no matching formula; the saturation makes the graph content too weak for the lead angle.
seed_details.red_team: This is missing-data arithmetic on a saturated graph.
seed_details.rebuttal: The formula is sharp and attained, but the objection correctly caps the seed below the broader exact-graph closure angle.

seed_details.opportunity: Characterize a selection-COPAG fiber constrained by observational and surrogate-intervention laws sharing one response-function model.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the single-regime moment map by coupled regime maps with common response tables and source masses but regime-specific selection normalizations.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for intervention-refined PAG bounds and surrogate-experiment sharp fibers found point-identification calculi and Yang et al.'s explicit future-work statement, but no attained shared-response fiber.
seed_details.red_team: This is Duarte et al. with more observed moment constraints.
seed_details.rebuttal: Separate regime programs are generally incompatible with one SCM, but exact-graph closure remains prior to the multi-regime extension and makes this seed less feasible than the chosen one.

seed_details.opportunity: Factor out every sIDP-identified component before bounding the residual nonidentified components of a discrete selection-COPAG query.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: When sIDP returns failure, retain its assembly-tree decomposition and send only unresolved leaf kernels to a shared response program.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing sIDP with sharp bounds located the paper's explicit open direction but no follow-up construction.
seed_details.red_team: This merely preprocesses Duarte et al.'s program with an identification algorithm.
seed_details.rebuttal: A completeness theorem for the residual program could be substantive, but without the exact-graph closure result it does not certify attained bounds and is therefore downstream of the chosen seed.

seed_details.anchor: LeeEtAl2023CardiacPAG, Methods and Limitations; ChangGuoMalinsky2026PostDiscovery, main coverage theorem
seed_details.opportunity: Construct graph-and-law confidence fibers for a selection-aware causal bound after FCI, including the zero-width boundary.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace graph-specific point-effect intervals by the union of compatibility-fiber images over resampled COPAGs and simultaneous multinomial regions.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for post-FCI set identification under selection found Gaussian point-effect post-discovery inference and generic identified-set inversion, but no selection-PAG confidence fiber.
seed_details.red_team: Coverage follows immediately from a union bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Finite-sample outer coverage is elementary, while informative shrinking graph sets and singular-face endpoint inference are occupied by unresolved assumptions; this is best retained as an inference rung, not the kernel.

seed_details.opportunity: Decide, rather than assume, whether a sharp bound over an exact graph stratum is a minimum or only an infimum.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Retain strict legality inequalities in the response program and apply quantifier elimination to the endpoint fiber instead of compact-simplex optimization.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for unattained causal bounds in exact graph strata and minimum-versus-infimum in automated bounds found no explicit criterion.
seed_details.red_team: Tarski--Seidenberg makes decidability formal and computationally vacuous.
seed_details.rebuttal: The criterion is a useful safety theorem and fallback, but without a structural lifting theorem it does not by itself justify a field-level paper.

seed_details.opportunity: Determine when two selected-marginalized directed graphs have identical quantitative compatibility fibers for every positive selected law and selection margin.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Strengthen Observe-and-Do model equality to equality of unnormalized selected moment maps and then test the converse with a separating bounded outcome.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for quantitative smDG fiber equivalence found structural indistinguishability only.
seed_details.red_team: Identical smDGs already imply the same interventional model by Carey et al.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their object conditions on selection and does not fix the absolute selection probabilities, but the quantitative converse is less directly tied to the clinical target than legal lifting.

literature_map.anchor_read: Evans's introduction, Theorem 4.13 proof, Proposition 7.3 proof, and discussion; Carey et al.'s introduction, canonical transformations, Proposition 11, and conclusion.
adjacent_threads: Duarte et al., Proposition 1, Theorem 1, Section 7, and the proof of Proposition 1: full-response discretization and fixed-graph polynomial bounds are settled.
Yang et al., Theorems 1--3 and Section 6: PAG-wide counterfactual expressiveness and neural bounding under faithfulness are settled without selection; intervention-refined classes remain open.
Boeken, Forré, and Mooij, Theorem 5 and Section 7: faithful distributions are open and dense in total variation, but equal-moment lifting on unfaithful faces is not addressed.
Chen and Mooij, Theorems 4.14--4.15 and Section 5: COPAG point identification under selection is complete; sharp discrete bounds are explicitly left open.
literature_map.occupancy_check: No inspected theorem preserves the triple consisting of the selected law's common normalization, the intervention-specific selection probability, and actual selected-MAG legality at response-mass boundaries.
literature_map.closest_non_subsuming: Carey et al. is structurally closer than Evans because it handles selection, but its equivalence is defined for normalized selected interventional models and therefore does not subsume the target moment fiber.

literature_map.anchor_read: Boeken, Forré, and Mooij's introduction, Theorem 5 proof strategy, and discussion; Yang et al.'s causal-diagram characterization and inducing-path constraints.
adjacent_threads: Richardson and Spirtes establish MAG closure under marginalization and conditioning, not parameter-stratum closure.
Yang et al. encode collider, noncollider, and inducing-path constraints with continuous masks, whose zero boundary changes the encoded graph.
Duarte et al. make fixed-architecture response laws polynomial, enabling exhaustive binary stratum analysis.
literature_map.occupancy_check: No paper inspected gives an iff endpoint-attainment frontier for a positive unfaithful law on the minimal compelled-collider COPAG.
literature_map.closest_non_subsuming: Boeken et al. characterize topological typicality of faithfulness rather than the image of an exact graph stratum under a causal moment map.

literature_map.anchor_read: Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe's introduction, Proposition 2 proof, consequences for closed semialgebraic sets, and conclusion; Duarte et al.'s Proposition 1 and its proof.
adjacent_threads: Evans merges latent vertices with nested observed child sets while preserving marginal causal models.
Duarte et al. bound full-response support for a fixed canonical DAG by preserving the full counterfactual law.
Yang et al. note exponentially many latent variables and more efficient inducing-path constraints as open scalability problems.
literature_map.occupancy_check: Existing support reductions preserve distributions or full potential-outcome laws for a fixed architecture, not the positivity of each functional-essentiality witness after architecture reduction.
literature_map.closest_non_subsuming: Duarte et al.'s full-response reduction is stronger than moment-only Carathéodory within a fixed canonical DAG, but it does not prove exact selected-MAG closure across a COPAG.

novelty_justification: {"adversarial_referee":"A skeptical referee will argue that either graph edges are merely allowed, making compactness routine, or actual edges are required, making the claim false by zero-mass limits. The project answers with an invariant essential-feature index, an if-and-only-if polynomial legality lemma including off-support functional dependence, a certificate that excludes all enumerated legal lifts, and an explicitly open universal lifting question.","bounded_search_result":"Primary-source searches through September 11, 2026, covering selection-aware PAG identification, PAG-constrained SCMs, selected-marginalized graph canonicalization, latent-cardinality reduction, fixed-graph autobounds, faithfulness topology, and post-discovery inference found no result that subsumes the exact graph-legal lifting question.","closest_results":["DuarteEtAl2024AutoBounds proves sharp polynomial-program equivalence for a supplied canonical DAG and includes selection examples.","YangEtAl2026PAGSCM proves PAG-wide counterfactual expressiveness and equality of neural and optimal PAG bounds under a faithful observational law."],"exact_gap":"The kernel retains actual functional dependence, unnormalized selection cells, calibrated population and interventional selection margins, and every selected MAG represented by a COPAG. These features create nonclosed legal strata; the new finite procedure returns an algebraic witness or a sign certificate, while equality with the arbitrary-SCM fiber remains the open lifting problem.","why_not_relabeling":"A fixed-graph polynomial program cannot certify that a boundary response law still induces the required graph, and a PAG mask program that assumes faithfulness excludes precisely the positive unfaithful laws where the closure problem arises."}
